units.function: Unit tests for turning Issue briefs or plugin-session messages into bounded, redacted structured wake payloads and adapter prompts.
units.dependencyDirection: Heartbeat payload builder reads optional Issue context and feeds adapter-utils prompt rendering; tests use minimal database stubs.
units.keyDataModels: Wake reason, truncated Issue summary, pluginKey/sessionId/source/text AgentMessage, fallbackFetchNeeded flag.
units.lifecycle: Include up to 12,000 characters of an Issue description and mark fallback fetch; render canonical gateway chat messages; return null for non-renderable timers; redact and bound session message text before prompt materialization.
units.testAssessment: Four focused cases cover truncation, canonical plugin message rendering, empty timer behavior and one credential-shape redaction. Missing are authorization/provenance, company/session binding, adversarial secret forms, Unicode boundaries, prompt injection, data classification/export policy, attachment handling and proof that fallback fetch is permission-scoped.
units.designRationale: Keep adapter wake prompts useful but bounded, and sanitize external session messages before they enter model context.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS must deliver human/Connector messages and Work briefs without leaking secrets or bypassing data authorization while preserving source attribution.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the typed bounded payload and explicit truncation/fetch receipt. Bind every message to principal, Company/Work, channel capability, data classification and original evidence hash; sanitize through Data/Evidence ports, and authorize any fallback fetch separately. Do not let plugin-private session IDs become core identity.
units.responsibilityConflict: The payload carries source/plugin/session labels but no authenticated human or Connector attestation, consent, data contract or prompt-injection policy; simple redaction cannot establish safe disclosure.

units.function: Pure tests deciding whether an actionable wake may move an assigned todo Issue into execution checkout.
units.dependencyDirection: Pure Heartbeat policy over wake context, Issue row status/assignee, dependency readiness and structured execution-review state.
units.keyDataModels: Issue todo status, Agent assignment, dependency readiness and current workflow stage/participant.
units.lifecycle: Auto-checkout ordinary dependency-ready assigned work, but do not convert a todo row that actually represents a pending review-stage participant.
units.testAssessment: Two cases capture the key regression but do not cover human participants, other stage types/status contradictions, reassignment races, approval, pause/cancel, atomic checkout or responsibility acceptance.
units.designRationale: Row status alone is insufficient; workflow execution state must prevent a reviewer wake from being mistaken for new implementation work.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS must distinguish Work ownership, workflow participation and execution authority so review/approval activity cannot accidentally grant an Agent executor rights.
units.companyOsFit: REFERENCE the state-projection consistency check. Company OS should make workflow stage and responsibility contract authoritative, with atomic capability-based checkout and explicit human/Agent role, rather than reconcile a generic todo field at dispatch time.
units.responsibilityConflict: The predicate checks Agent identity and workflow stage but not accountable-human acceptance or an execution/approval/data capability receipt.

units.function: Pure tests classifying token-bearing usage as reported or unpriced and selecting cache-adjusted provider cost for ledger billing.
units.dependencyDirection: Pure Heartbeat helpers over adapter-reported numeric usage/cost fields.
units.keyDataModels: Input/cached/output token counts, nominal costUsd, cacheAdjustedCostUsd and ledger cost status.
units.lifecycle: Prefer a finite cache-adjusted cost, otherwise use provider cost; mark token usage without cost unpriced and any available billed amount reported.
units.testAssessment: Seven concise cases cover missing/reported/cache-adjusted combinations and NaN. Missing are negative/infinite/overflow values, currency and precision, provider/model/pricing version, estimated versus invoiced reconciliation, retries/deduplication, cache-write charges and signed usage provenance.
units.designRationale: Avoid silently treating substantial CLI token use as free and use the provider's discounted billed amount when available.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs trustworthy cross-provider cost governance and budget reservations without conflating telemetry, estimates and settled charges.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the explicit unpriced state, not the numeric helper. Define Money/currency, UsageReceipt provenance, pricing version, estimated/reported/settled states, idempotent attempt key and reconciliation; BudgetPort reserves before execution and settles from verified Connector/provider evidence.
units.responsibilityConflict: Unverified adapter numbers directly influence ledger semantics, with no responsible owner, pricing contract or evidence signature; a reported value is not necessarily a settled enterprise charge.

units.function: Unit tests resolving an Issue-scoped billing code and Project into the cost-ledger scope for a Run.
units.dependencyDirection: Heartbeat ledger helper queries the Company-visible Issue referenced by Run context and otherwise falls back to the context Project.
units.keyDataModels: Run context Issue/Project IDs, Issue projectId/billingCode and ledger scope.
units.lifecycle: Use authoritative Issue Project and billing code when visible in the Company; return null Issue/billing code and context Project when absent or cross-Company.
units.testAssessment: Four cases cover present/null/no-Issue/cross-Company lookup and no-query optimization. Missing are billing-code mutation timing, archived/deleted Work, Project/company mismatch, authorization, immutable Run snapshot, invoice export and structured cost-center contracts.
units.designRationale: Attribute execution cost to the Work's current business billing dimension while preserving tenant isolation.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS must carry cost center/project/customer attribution into immutable execution and settlement evidence for FDE and enterprise finance workflows.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT by resolving a versioned CostAllocationContract before execution and copying its immutable ID/digest onto the attempt and usage receipts. Do not re-read a mutable Issue billingCode at settlement time.
units.responsibilityConflict: A mutable Issue field is not proof that an accountable budget owner approved the allocation, and null fallback can silently produce unattributed spend.
